title: Whiteboard W3: keep or revert the ledger hot-path changes e2440a6, bd0c17d and 3884493 on the #196 line
problem: Whiteboard item W3 (board #96, comment 6852550499) asks whether the three commits that make a body tick read only new history should stay on #196. They change how the evidence ledger, the event spine and the mission book read retained records. The whiteboard names the #196 integrator as owner of the call. This record is self-review: one session (session_01FBS4KNJR59nSbdGbxo8Mbx) wrote all five roles.
founder_intent_refs: INTENT-20261112-CONVERGENCE-USEFUL-PATH (whiteboard authority note, founder reply 'Approved', #96 comment 6852618695)
INTENT-20261001-FULL-MACHINE-COMPLETION (a body that persists across months)
CONTRADICTION-0002 Option A (live constitutional integrity is separate from historical continuity pins)
baseline: #196 at f383fd26 carries all three commits. Canonical CI on f383fd26 passes every job (job 1: the full kernel and organ suite; jobs 10 and 10b: every mutation gate). #211 (bounded body memory, adopted at 50cf3f75) is built on the incremental spine and ledger indexes that these commits introduced.

alternatives.name: Revert all three
alternatives.description: Restore whole-chain re-verification and whole-history replay on every append, read and rebuild.
advantages: Every read re-hashes the whole chain, so an in-process alteration of the ledger's private list is caught on the next read instead of within 300 s.
disadvantages: A body tick grows with history again: about 3 s per tick at 7,800 records, 136.8 ms at 31,256 for one holding mission (measured in the commit messages).
It breaks #211's bounded-memory ledger, which reads payloads back by position from the indexes.
It discards tested work: tests/unit/test_greg_mission_book_incremental.py checks every rebuild against a fresh fold.
alternatives.revival_evidence: A demonstrated correctness defect in the incremental paths (an answer that differs from a full replay) that a targeted fix cannot close.

alternatives.name: Keep, and also apply the three-line Gate claim-lookup change
alternatives.description: Retain the commits and change policy/consequence_gate.py so its claim scan uses the ledger index (8.2 ms flat instead of 18.0 ms).
advantages: Removes the last term of tick time that grows with history.
disadvantages: policy/consequence_gate.py is a continuity artifact pinned by the repair harness (SR002); a first version that changed it failed 13 repair-harness tests and was reverted.
alternatives.revival_evidence: Whiteboard W4 concludes that the pin can move without weakening what it attests. W4 is claimed separately (#96 comment by session_012cg2bknzWBFYr1ZucX4Bru).

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: The commits stay where they are on #196 (do nothing equals retain here).
advantages: No churn; CI is green on the current tree.
disadvantages: Without a recorded decision, W3 stays open on the whiteboard and the 300 s detection window stays undocumented as an accepted risk.

roles.position: A body that runs for months with a bounded tick is part of the full machine. Reverting would move the line away from it.
material_concerns: The founder's merge decision (W2) should see a line whose tick does not grow with history.
evidence_refs: e2440a6 commit message: 3 s per tick at 7,800 records before
3884493 commit message: 18.0 ms at 31,256 records after

roles.position: The incremental indexes are now load-bearing: #211's bounded memory and the mission book's incremental fold read through them.
material_concerns: Two readers of one ledger must agree. The indexes re-check each answer against the record before handing it out.

roles.position: The weakest point is detection latency: code inside the process that alters the ledger's private list can be served for up to 300 s before a full re-verification.
material_concerns: The window is real, but it needs code already inside the process, which can do worse than that. Every explicit verify_chain() and every reopen still checks the whole chain.
evidence_refs: e2440a6 commit message, 'Given up, stated plainly'

roles.position: Full CI is green on the current tree with these commits; the whiteboard's earlier 49-against-48 failure comparison is superseded by zero failures.
material_concerns: A future change to the ledger must keep the incremental paths and the full re-verification in step.
evidence_refs: Canonical CI on f383fd26: every job success

roles.position: No evidence is dropped: retained records never leave the ledger, and readers get copies, so a reader's bug cannot alter history.
material_concerns: Evidence-retention questions belong to W5 and #278 (compaction), which this decision does not settle.
evidence_refs: e2440a6: every read hands out the caller's own copy

evidence.claim: The full kernel and organ suite and every mutation gate pass with the commits applied
An incremental mission-book rebuild equals a fresh fold
evidence.finding: eight real mission scenarios checked at every rebuild; 10 of 10 applicable mutants caught

evidence.claim: Tick time no longer grows with history except the Gate claim scan
evidence.finding: median active tick 136.8 ms -> 18.0 ms at 31,256 records

counterevidence.claim: Detection of an in-process alteration is delayed
counterevidence.finding: up to 300 s on the hot path; explicit verify_chain() and reopen catch it at once

counterevidence.claim: Tick time still grows slowly through the Gate's claim scan
counterevidence.finding: 8.2 ms flat only with the unapplied Gate change (W4)

pass_1.intended_outcome: A body's tick cost stays bounded as its history grows, with no change to what history says or to whole-chain verification on open and on request.

advantages.statement: Tick cost no longer scales with retained records on the mission and observation paths.
advantages.amplified_value: Makes month-long founder-device operation practical and is the base #211's bounded memory builds on.

advantages.statement: Readers receive copies, so a reader's bug cannot corrupt history.
advantages.amplified_value: Turns a whole class of evidence corruption into a non-event.

disadvantages.statement: Up to 300 s before an in-process alteration of the ledger's private list is noticed on the hot path.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep whole-chain verification on open, on every explicit verify_chain(), on assigned history and every 300 s; document the window as an accepted risk.

disadvantages.statement: Two code paths (incremental and full) must stay consistent.
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Keep the tests that compare each incremental answer with a full replay; any ledger change must keep them passing.

comparisons.baseline: #196 with the commits: green CI, bounded tick.
comparisons.do_nothing: Same as the baseline; the decision is only recorded.
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: Revert: simpler code paths, but tick cost grows with history and #211 breaks.
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: Keep and also change the Gate claim scan (W4), blocked on the SR002 continuity pin.
comparisons.reversible_experiment: None needed: the effect is already measured, and a revert stays possible by git revert of the three commits plus #211.

rejected_alternatives.name: Revert all three
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Reintroduces growth with history and breaks adopted work, with no correctness defect shown.
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: A reproduced incremental-versus-full disagreement that a targeted fix cannot close.

pass_2.attack_summary: Attacked the strengthened design for a reader that bypasses the indexes, a fold that silently skips a record, and hidden dependence of other work on these commits.

new_weaknesses.statement: Later work (#211 and the bounded payload store) now depends on these indexes, so a future revert is no longer a three-commit operation.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: Record the dependency here and in the #196 body, so a revert decision sees its full cost.

new_weaknesses.statement: The 300 s window is documented only in a commit message.
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: This record states it as an accepted risk with an owner and a review trigger.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: The attacker needs code inside the process, and full verification still runs on open, on request and every 300 s.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any change that lets untrusted code run in the body's process, or a finding that the 300 s full check can be skipped.

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: Equivalence tests exist and run in job 1, which is green.
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: Any change to provenance/ledger.py, events/spine.py or MissionBook.rebuild.

pass_2.final_design: RETAIN e2440a6, bd0c17d and 3884493 on #196 as they are. The Gate claim-scan change stays with W4. Compaction and memory policy stay with W5 and #278.

residual_risks.risk: A future ledger change updates one path and not the other.
residual_risks.mitigation: The incremental-versus-replay tests fail on such a change.
residual_risks.review_trigger: Any change to the ledger or spine read paths.

residual_risks.risk: The 300 s window is exploited by in-process code.
residual_risks.mitigation: Explicit verify_chain() before any consequential export or acceptance read.
residual_risks.review_trigger: A new in-process plugin or worker model.

dissent.handling: No role dissented. This is self-review by one session; any agent may reopen W3 on #96 with a reproduced incremental-versus-full disagreement.

migration_plan: None: the commits are already on #196. This record documents the decision and the accepted risk.

steps: git revert 3884493e bd0c17dc e2440a64 on #196 after first reverting or adapting #211's bounded payload store
Re-run job 1 and the mission-book incremental tests

kill_criteria: A reproduced case where an incremental ledger, spine or mission-book answer differs from a full replay and cannot be fixed in place
decision_owner: #196 integrator, session_01FBS4KNJR59nSbdGbxo8Mbx (named owner of W3 on the whiteboard)
review_trigger: Any change to provenance/ledger.py, events/spine.py or MissionBook.rebuild; the W4 outcome; the W5/#278 outcome.
